title: InVideo Review 2026: What Can You Actually Do With It?
rawContent:
Quick Blog Summary

I spent time testing InVideo, going through its AI tools, the pricing and what other users are saying online. In this review, I’ll walk you through what the platform actually does, how video, image and audio generation work, what InVideo Studio offers, the real pricing plans and the honest pros and cons. If you just want the short version: InVideo is a good tool if you want nice looking videos without knowing how to edit, but the credit pricing can surprise you if you’re not paying attention. Let’s get into the details.

What is InVideo

InVideo has been around since 2017. It started as a simple video editor with templates, the kind where you pick a design, drop in your clips and export. Nothing fancy, just useful. Once AI video tools started getting popular, InVideo added a second product on top of the old one. Now there are two parts to it, both under the same account.

InVideo Studio is the original editor. You drag and drop your clips, pick templates, add stock footage, text and music and build the video by hand. InVideo AI is the newer part and honestly the one everyone talks about now. You type out what kind of video you want and it writes the script, picks the visuals, adds a voiceover and puts captions on it, all on its own.

You don’t have to pick one or the other. You can start with AI to get a rough video out fast, then jump into Studio if you want to clean it up yourself.

Quick Features Overview

Here’s the short version of everything you’re actually paying for:

  • Video generation with Sora 2, VEO 3.1, Kling 3.0, Seedance 2.0, plus the Agent One editing feature
  • Image generation using Nano Banana Pro and Seedream
  • Audio generation powered by ElevenLabs, including voice cloning in about 18 languages
  • AI avatars through the AI Twin feature
  • InVideo Studio for manual editing, with templates, stock footage, and a brand kit
  • Multi-format export, team features, mobile apps, and auto captions with translation
  • Commercial rights and watermark-free exports on every paid plan

InVideo Video Generation

We tested the InVideo AI Video Generator with real prompts and shared the results, features, pros, cons, and pricing. Check out the full review.

👉 Try InVideo AI Video Generator

This is the part that gets the most attention and honestly it’s what makes InVideo worth talking about in 2026.

Instead of picking a template and filling in the blanks, you just describe the video you want in a sentence or two, and it builds something from that. Behind the scenes, it’s using some of the best video models out there right now, VEO 3.1, Sora 2, Kling 3.0, and Seedance 2.0. Normally, getting access to something like Sora 2 or VEO 3.1 on their own would cost you a lot more every month. Having all of them in one place is the real reason people use InVideo. If you want to see how it stacks up against other options first, check out our best AI video generators guide. 

The feature I found most interesting is called Agent One. You give it one prompt and it can put together up to 30 minutes of video. If you want to change something after, you don’t have to touch a timeline. You just type what you want, something like “make the intro shorter” or “change the background music,” and it does it for you.

Autopilot Mode vs Agent Mode

Once you start using InVideo, you’ll notice it gives you two different ways to create a video and it helps to know the difference before you pick one.

The first is Autopilot Mode, basically one-click video creation. You type a prompt or an idea and the AI takes over from there, it writes the script, picks the visuals, adds voiceover, subtitles and music and hands you a finished video in seconds. You’re not making creative decisions here, the AI is. This is great when you just want a quick YouTube Short, an Instagram Reel or a simple social ad and you don’t want to spend time editing anything.

The second is Agent Mode, also called Agent One, and this one works more like you’re the director and the AI is your assistant. You get to plan the script and storyboard, and direct the video scene by scene. You can pick specific AI models like VEO, Kling, or Sora, keep character appearances consistent across scenes, adjust camera angles, and fine-tune the exact look you’re going for. This is the one to use for short films, storytelling, brand videos, or anything where you actually care about how each frame looks.

Here’s a quick way to think about which one fits you:

If you’re in a hurry and just need something decent out fast, go Autopilot. If you actually care about how the final video looks and want to control the details, Agent Mode is worth the extra time.

There’s also an avatar feature called AI Twin. You can clone your own face and voice or pick from a library of digital presenters, so you don’t have to be on camera yourself. This is handy for ads, course videos or social content where you’d rather not show your face.

InVideo Image Generation

Along with video, InVideo lets you generate images too, not just pull stock photos.

It uses Nano Banana Pro from Google DeepMind and Seedream from ByteDance, both solid image models. You can make thumbnails, backgrounds, product shots or custom visuals right inside the same tool you’re using to build your video, so you’re not switching between five different apps to get one project done.

This matters if you’re tired of the same recycled stock footage everyone else is using and want something that actually looks different. If you want to compare it with other tools before deciding, our best AI image generator guide covers that. 

InVideo Audio Generation

Audio covers your voiceover, background music and sound effects and this is honestly one of the stronger parts of the platform.

The voice generation runs on ElevenLabs, which is widely known for sounding natural rather than robotic. You get voiceovers in multiple languages, and you can even clone your own voice so a video sounds like you narrated it without you actually recording anything. Voice cloning covers around 18 languages with different accents, though it still doesn’t quite match the emotion range of a real voice actor. If voice quality matters a lot to you, it’s worth checking our best AI voice generators guide to see how it compares. 

For music and sound effects, you get a licensed stock library built in, so you don’t have to worry about copyright issues later.

InVideo Studio

Studio is for people who’d rather have full control instead of letting AI make all the decisions.

It’s a normal drag and drop editor with a big template library for social posts, ads and YouTube intros. You get stock footage, images and music through a Storyblocks partnership and you can export in different formats like 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1, so the same project works for YouTube, Reels and Shorts without redoing anything. There’s also a brand kit to save your logo, colors and fonts, team features if you’re working with others, auto captions with translation and a mobile app for iOS and Android.

If you already have footage to work with, or your AI-generated video needs some manual touch-ups before you post it, Studio is where you’d do that. If you specifically need to clean up or edit images before adding them, our best AI image editors guide can help you pick the right one. 

InVideo Pricing Plan

There’s a free plan, but it comes with a watermark and very limited AI usage each week. It’s fine for testing things out, not for anything you actually want to publish.

Here’s how the paid plans break down, based on annual billing:

👉 Explore InVideo Pricing

A few things I noticed that actually matter here. Every paid plan gives you access to the same 200+ AI models, including Seedance 2.0, VEO 3.1, Kling 3.0, Nano Banana Pro and ElevenLabs music. The plans don’t differ by what models you can use, they differ by how many credits you get, how many avatars and voice clones you can make, how much storage you have and how many things you can generate at the same time. Max gives you double the concurrency of Plus, Generative gives 10 times more and Elite gives 20 times more. If you’re the type who runs several generations at once, that matters more than the credit number itself.

To give you a sense of how far credits go, InVideo says 75 credits, the Plus plan, covers about 300 Nano Banana Pro images or 600 Nano Banana 2 images. That scales up through the tiers, so Elite’s 4,250 credits covers around 17,000 Nano Banana Pro images or 34,000 Nano Banana 2 images, if you spent them all on images. In real use, video generation with something like Sora 2 or VEO 3.1 burns through credits much faster than images do, so treat these numbers as a rough ceiling, not what you’ll actually get every month.

All paid plans let you export without a watermark, and give you access to stock providers like iStock and Storyblocks. If you run out of credits mid-month, you can buy more on demand, which is good to know since unused credits don’t carry over to the next month. Also worth mentioning, InVideo says model and agent prices can change, so it’s smart to check their pricing page before you commit.

What Real Users Are Saying

I went through a bunch of reviews online to see what people actually experience, not just what the marketing says.

On the good side, people say the interface is easy to learn even if you’ve never edited a video before. The templates and stock library get a lot of praise. Voice cloning and auto captions come up often as real time savers. A few people also mentioned the chat support being patient and actually solving their problem.

On the not so good side, the credit system is the biggest complaint by far. Some users said credits got taken even when a video failed to render properly. A few mentioned Agent One using up way more credits than they expected, which led to surprise charges. Some felt the output quality wasn’t always consistent, especially on the cheaper plans. Support response times were mixed too, some people got quick help, others got copy-paste answers that didn’t fix anything. A handful also said some AI features they were promised weren’t fully working after they paid.

Basically, most people agree the tool works and has real potential, but the pricing and credit system are what actually annoy people the most.

Pros and Cons

What I liked 

You get access to over 200 AI models, including Sora 2 and VEO 3.1, all in one place. There’s a free plan so you can try it before spending anything. It’s easy to use even with zero editing experience. The template and stock library is genuinely large. Exporting for different platforms is simple. It works well for teams too, with brand kits and shared projects. Voice cloning and captions are solid.

What bugged me

The credit system takes some getting used to, and you can lose credits on a failed generation. Credits don’t carry over if you don’t use them. Heavy AI use can get expensive fast. Output quality isn’t always consistent. Support experience depends on who you get. The higher plans cost more than some other tools out there.

Frequently Asked Questions


1. Can I use InVideo for free?

Yes, but the free plan has a watermark and limited AI usage per week. Good enough to test, not enough to publish something serious.


2. Is InVideo AI better than other video tools?

Depends what you’re doing. If you want to generate videos from a prompt using models like Sora 2 and VEO 3.1, it’s one of the strongest options. If you already have footage to edit or you need a really polished avatar specifically, a more specialized tool might do that one thing better.


3. How do the credits actually work?

Every time you generate something with AI, video, image or voice, it uses credits from your monthly pool. Credits reset every month and whatever you don’t use doesn’t roll over.


4. Can I use the videos for business or commercial stuff?

Yes, every paid plan includes commercial rights and lets you export without a watermark.


5. Is it hard to learn?

No. Between the AI prompt option and the drag and drop editor, you don’t need any prior experience to make something usable.


6. What’s the actual difference between InVideo AI and InVideo Studio?

InVideo AI builds a full video from a text prompt, including the script and voiceover. InVideo Studio is the manual editor where you build or fine-tune things yourself. Both come with the same account.

My Final Take

InVideo is an all-in-one AI platform that lets you create videos, images and audio. It also includes a full video editor, so you can edit your projects in one place. One subscription gives you access to multiple AI models, such as Sora and Veo, so you don’t need to pay for each model separately.

To get the best results, write clear and detailed prompts. If your prompt is too vague, the output will usually be poor. Also, think about what you want before generating because every new generation uses credits.

If you’re new to InVideo, start with the free plan. Once you understand how many credits you use, you can decide if a paid plan is worth it. It’s a great choice for creating social media content, but if you make videos every day for work, keep an eye on your credit usage so you don’t run out too quickly.
